sanskrit: ity uktasya yathānyāyaṃ rāvaṇasya jaṭāyuṣā kruddhasyāgninibhāḥ sarvā rejur viṃśatidṛṣṭayaḥ
english: When Rāvaṇa was thus rightly addressed by Jaṭāyu, all twenty eyes of that enraged one blazed like fire.

sanskrit: saṃraktanayanaḥ kopāt taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ rākṣasendro 'bhidudrāva patagendram amarṣaṇaḥ
english: His eyes crimson with rage, his earrings of heated gold swinging, the lord of rākṣasas, overcome with fury, rushed at the king of birds.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulas tayos tasmin mahāvane babhūva vātoddhatayor meghayor gagane yathā
english: The collision between those two in that great forest was tumultuous, like that of two storm-driven clouds clashing in the sky.

sanskrit: tad babhūvādbhutaṃ yuddhaṃ gṛdhrarākṣasayos tadā sapakṣayor mālyavator mahāparvatayor iva
english: That battle between the vulture and the rākṣasa was wondrous, like that of two mighty winged mountains, the Mālyavat peaks.

sanskrit: tato nālīkanārācais tīkṣṇāgraiś ca vikarṇibhiḥ abhyavarṣan mahāghorair gṛdhrarājaṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Then the mighty one rained upon the king of vultures arrows — nālīkas, nārācas, and vikarṇis with sharp tips — all exceedingly fearsome.

sanskrit: sa tāni śarajālāni gṛdhra patraratheśvaraḥ jaṭāyuḥ pratijagrāha rāvaṇāstrāṇi saṃyuge
english: Jaṭāyu, the lord of birds that ride on wings, intercepted those showers of arrows, those weapons of Rāvaṇa, in the battle.

sanskrit: tasya tīkṣṇanakhābhyāṃ tu caraṇābhyāṃ mahābalaḥ cakāra bahudhā gātre vraṇān patagasattamaḥ
english: With his two feet armed with sharp talons, that most excellent of birds, immensely powerful, slashed many wounds all over Rāvaṇa's body.

sanskrit: atha krodhād daśagrīvo jagrāha daśamārgaṇān mṛtyudaṇḍanibhān ghorāñ śatrumardanakāṅkṣayā
english: Then Daśagrīva, burning with anger and longing to crush his foe, seized ten terrible arrows resembling the staff of Death.

sanskrit: sa tair bāṇair mahāvīryaḥ pūrṇamuktair ajihmagaiḥ bibheda niśitais tīkṣṇair gṛdhraṃ ghoraiḥ śilīmukhaiḥ
english: With those arrows — drawn to the full, flying straight, sharp-tipped, and terrifying — that exceedingly mighty one pierced the vulture.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasarathe paśyañ jānakīṃ bāṣpalocanām acintayitvā bāṇāṃs tān rākṣasaṃ samabhidravat
english: Seeing Jānakī on the rākṣasa's chariot, her eyes filled with tears, he gave no thought to those arrows and charged straight at the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tato 'sya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ muktāmaṇivibhūṣitam caraṇābhyāṃ mahātejā babhañja patageśvaraḥ
english: Then with his two feet, that most radiant lord of birds shattered his arrow-set bow, adorned with pearls and gems.

sanskrit: tac cāgnisadṛśaṃ dīptaṃ rāvaṇasya śarāvaram pakṣābhyāṃ ca mahātejā vyadhunot patageśvaraḥ
english: And with his wings, that most radiant lord of birds scattered Rāvaṇa's quiver of arrows that blazed like fire.

sanskrit: kāñcanoraśchadān divyān piśācavadanān kharān tāṃś cāsya javasaṃpannāñ jaghāna samare balī
english: The mighty one also slew in battle his fleet mules — those divine, swift animals with golden trappings and demon-like faces.

sanskrit: varaṃ triveṇusaṃpannaṃ kāmagaṃ pāvakārciṣam maṇihemavicitrāṅgaṃ babhañja ca mahāratham pūrṇacandrapratīkāśaṃ chatraṃ ca vyajanaiḥ saha
english: He also smashed the magnificent chariot — fitted with its triple shaft, going at will, blazing like fire, beautifully adorned with gems and gold — and likewise the parasol resembling the full moon, together with the fly-whisks.

sanskrit: sa bhagnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ aṅkenādāya vaidehīṃ papāta bhuvi rāvaṇaḥ
english: His bow shattered, his chariot wrecked, his horses slain, his charioteer killed, Rāvaṇa fell to the ground, clutching Vaidehī in his lap.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā nipatitaṃ bhūmau rāvaṇaṃ bhagnavāhanam sādhu sādhv iti bhūtāni gṛdhrarājam apūjayan
english: Seeing Rāvaṇa fallen on the ground with his vehicle destroyed, all beings praised the king of vultures, crying "Bravo! Bravo!"

sanskrit: pariśrāntaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā jarayā pakṣiyūthapam utpapāta punar hṛṣṭo maithilīṃ gṛhya rāvaṇaḥ
english: But seeing that leader of the bird host exhausted by old age, Rāvaṇa leaped up again with renewed vigour, seizing Maithilī.

sanskrit: taṃ prahṛṣṭaṃ nidhāyāṅke gacchantaṃ janakātmajām gṛdhrarājaḥ samutpatya jaṭāyur idam abravīt
english: Seeing him joyfully bearing the daughter of Janaka away in his lap, the king of vultures, Jaṭāyu, soared up and spoke these words.

sanskrit: vajrasaṃsparśabāṇasya bhāryāṃ rāmasya rāvaṇa alpabuddhe harasy enāṃ vadhāya khalu rakṣasām
english: "O Rāvaṇa, O dim-witted one, you carry off the wife of Rāma, whose arrows strike like the thunderbolt — this is truly for the destruction of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: samitrabandhuḥ sāmātyaḥ sabalaḥ saparicchadaḥ viṣapānaṃ pibasy etat pipāsita ivodakam
english: "Together with your allies and kinsmen, your ministers, your army, and your retinue, you drink this poison as a thirsty man drinks water."

sanskrit: anubandham ajānantaḥ karmaṇām avicakṣaṇāḥ śīghram eva vinaśyanti yathā tvaṃ vinaśiṣyasi
english: "Those who are heedless and do not perceive the consequence of their actions quickly perish — just as you shall perish."

sanskrit: baddhas tvaṃ kālapāśena kva gatas tasya mokṣyase vadhāya baḍiśaṃ gṛhya sāmiṣaṃ jalajo yathā
english: "You are bound in the noose of Time — wherever you go, how will you escape it? Like a water-creature that swallows a baited hook and is caught for slaughter."

sanskrit: na hi jātu durādharṣau kākutsthau tava rāvaṇa dharṣaṇaṃ cāśramasyāsya kṣamiṣyete tu rāghavau
english: "The two Kākutsthas are never to be assailed, O Rāvaṇa; the Rāghavas will never tolerate this violation of their hermitage."

sanskrit: yathā tvayā kṛtaṃ karma bhīruṇā lokagarhitam taskarācarito mārgo naiṣa vīraniṣevitaḥ
english: "The deed you have done, O coward, is censured by the world. This is the path of a thief — it is not the way trodden by heroes."

sanskrit: yudhyasva yadi śūro 'si muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha rāvaṇa śayiṣyase hato bhūmau yathā bhrātā kharas tathā
english: "Fight if you are a hero — stand a moment, O Rāvaṇa! You shall lie slain on the ground just as your brother Khara did."

sanskrit: paretakāle puruṣo yat karma pratipadyate vināśāyātmano 'dharmyaṃ pratipanno 'si karma tat
english: "The deed that a man embarks on at the hour of his doom is one leading to his own destruction, one contrary to dharma — and that is the deed you have undertaken."

sanskrit: pāpānubandho vai yasya karmaṇaḥ ko nu tat pumān kurvīta lokādhipatiḥ svayambhūr bhagavān api
english: "Who then would carry out that action whose consequence is sin? Not even the lord of the worlds, the blessed Svayambhū, would do it."

sanskrit: evam uktvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ jaṭāyus tasya rakṣasaḥ nipapāta bhṛśaṃ pṛṣṭhe daśagrīvasya vīryavān
english: Having spoken those righteous words to that rākṣasa, the valiant Jaṭāyu fell with great force upon the back of Daśagrīva.

sanskrit: taṃ gṛhītvā nakhais tīkṣṇair virarāda samantataḥ adhirūḍho gajārohi yathā syād duṣṭavāraṇam
english: Seizing him and raking him all over with sharp talons, he mounted him as a mahout mounts a rogue elephant.

sanskrit: virarāda nakhair asya tuṇḍaṃ pṛṣṭhe samarpayan keśāṃś cotpāṭayām āsa nakhapakṣamukhāyudhaḥ
english: He tore at him with his talons, burying his beak into his back, and tore out his hair — Jaṭāyu, who fights with talons, wings, and beak as weapons.

sanskrit: sa tathā gṛdhrarājena kliśyamāno muhur muhuḥ amarṣasphuritauṣṭhaḥ san prākampata sa rākṣasaḥ
english: Tormented again and again by the king of vultures in this way, that rākṣasa trembled, his lips quivering with indignation.

sanskrit: saṃpariṣvajya vaidehīṃ vāmenāṅkena rāvaṇaḥ talenābhijaghānārto jaṭāyuṃ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa, clasping Vaidehī in his left arm, overwhelmed by pain and overcome with rage, struck Jaṭāyu with his open palm.

sanskrit: jaṭāyus tam atikramya tuṇḍenāsya kharādhipaḥ vāmabāhūn daśa tadā vyapāharad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Jaṭāyu, that subduer of foes and master of harsh deeds, turning on him with his beak, then severed all ten of his left arms.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho daśakrīvaḥ sītām utsṛjya vīryavān muṣṭibhyāṃ caraṇābhyāṃ ca gṛdhrarājam apothayat
english: Then Daśagrīva, enraged and powerful, releasing Sītā, pounded the king of vultures with fists and feet.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtaṃ saṃgrāmo babhūvātulavīryayoḥ rākṣasānāṃ ca mukhyasya pakṣiṇāṃ pravarasya ca
english: For a moment a battle raged between those two of incomparable might — the foremost of rākṣasas and the greatest of birds.

sanskrit: tasya vyāyacchamānasya rāmasyārthe 'tha rāvaṇaḥ pakṣau pādau ca pārśvau ca khaḍgam uddhṛtya so 'cchinat
english: As he strained himself on Rāma's behalf, Rāvaṇa drew his sword and cut off his wings, his feet, and his flanks.

sanskrit: sa chinnapakṣaḥ sahasā rakṣasā raudrakarmaṇā nipapāta hato gṛdhro dharaṇyām alpajīvitaḥ
english: His wings severed by that rākṣasa of terrible deeds, the vulture suddenly fell slain to the earth, barely alive.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau kṣatajārdraṃ jaṭāyuṣam abhyadhāvata vaidehī svabandhum iva duḥkhitā
english: Seeing Jaṭāyu fallen on the ground soaked in blood, Vaidehī ran toward him in grief, as toward her own kinsman.

sanskrit: taṃ nīlajīmūtanikāśakalpaṃ supāṇḍuroraskam udāravīryam dadarśa laṅkādhipatiḥ pṛthivyāṃ jaṭāyuṣaṃ śāntam ivāgnidāvam
english: The lord of Laṅkā beheld Jaṭāyu lying on the earth — dark as a blue storm-cloud in form, his breast very pale, his valour noble, quiescent as a forest-fire that has burned out.

sanskrit: tatas tu taṃ patrarathaṃ mahītale nipātitaṃ rāvaṇavegamarditam punaḥ pariṣvajya śaśiprabhānanā ruroda sītā janakātmajā tadā
english: Then Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, whose face shone like the moon, embraced once more that bird who rides on wings, lying struck down on the ground and crushed by Rāvaṇa's violence, and wept.

sanskrit: tam alpajīvitaṃ bhūmau sphurantaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ dadarśa gṛdhraṃ patitaṃ samīpe rāghavāśramāt
english: The lord of rākṣasas saw the vulture fallen on the ground, barely alive and quivering, near the hermitage of the Rāghavas.

sanskrit: sā tu tārādhipamukhī rāvaṇena samīkṣya tam gṛdhrarājaṃ vinihataṃ vilalāpa suduḥkhitā
english: She whose face was like the lord of stars, looking upon that king of vultures slain by Rāvaṇa, lamented in the deepest grief.

sanskrit: nimittaṃ lakṣaṇajñānaṃ śakunisvaradarśanam avaśyaṃ sukhaduḥkheṣu narāṇāṃ pratidṛśyate
english: "Omens, knowledge of portents, and the sound and sight of birds are invariably manifest for men in matters of happiness and sorrow."

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ rāma jānāsi mahad vyasanam ātmajaḥ dhāvanti nūnaṃ kākutstha madarthaṃ mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
english: "Surely, O Rāma, you do not know of the great calamity, O son. Surely, O Kākutstha, the beasts and birds are running on my behalf."

sanskrit: trāhi mām adya kākutstha lakṣmaṇeti varāṅganā susaṃtrastā samākrandac chṛṇvatāṃ tu yathāntike
english: "Save me today, O Kākutstha! O Lakṣmaṇa!" — the most excellent of women cried out in uttermost terror, so that those nearby could hear.

sanskrit: tāṃ kliṣṭamālyābharaṇāṃ vilapantīm anāthavat abhyadhāvata vaidehīṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, rushed at Vaidehī, her garlands and ornaments dishevelled, lamenting like one without a protector.

sanskrit: tāṃ latām iva veṣṭantīm āliṅgantīṃ mahādrumān muñca muñceti bahuśaḥ pravadan rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: As she clung like a creeper winding around the great trees, the lord of rākṣasas repeatedly called out "Let go, let go!"

sanskrit: krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti rāmeṇa rahitāṃ vane jīvitāntāya keśeṣu jagrāhāntakasaṃnibhaḥ
english: As she cried out "Rāma! Rāma!" — bereft of Rāma in the forest — he who resembled Death seized her by the hair to end her life.

sanskrit: pradharṣitāyāṃ vaidehyāṃ babhūva sacarācaram jagat sarvam amaryādaṃ tamasāndhena saṃvṛtam
english: When Vaidehī was thus violated, the entire world, moving and unmoving, became lawless and was shrouded in blinding darkness.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā sītāṃ parāmṛṣṭāṃ dīnāṃ divyena cakṣuṣā kṛtaṃ kāryam iti śrīmān vyājahāra pitāmahaḥ
english: Seeing Sītā seized and wretched with his divine eye, the illustrious Pitāmaha declared: "The purpose is accomplished."

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭā vyathitāś cāsan sarve te paramarṣayaḥ dṛṣṭvā sītāṃ parāmṛṣṭāṃ daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinaḥ
english: All the great sages dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, beholding Sītā thus seized, were simultaneously filled with joy and anguish.

sanskrit: sa tu tāṃ rāma rāmeti rudantīṃ lakṣmaṇeti ca jagāmākāśam ādāya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: And Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, carrying her away into the sky as she wept calling "Rāma! Rāma! Lakṣmaṇa!", departed.

sanskrit: taptābharaṇasarvāṅgī pītakauśeyavāsanī rarāja rājaputrī tu vidyut saudāmanī yathā
english: The princess, all her limbs adorned with burnished ornaments and clad in a yellow silk garment, shone like a flash of lightning named Saudāmanī.

sanskrit: uddhūtena ca vastreṇa tasyāḥ pītena rāvaṇaḥ adhikaṃ paribabhrāja girir dīpa ivāgninā
english: With her yellow garment streaming in the wind, Rāvaṇa shone all the more gloriously, like a mountain lit by a lamp of fire.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ paramakalyāṇyās tāmrāṇi surabhīṇi ca padmapatrāṇi vaidehyā abhyakīryanta rāvaṇam
english: The coppery, fragrant lotus petals of that most auspicious Vaidehī scattered and fell upon Rāvaṇa all around.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ kauśeyam uddhūtam ākāśe kanakaprabham babhau cādityarāgeṇa tāmram abhram ivātape
english: Her silk garment, streaming in the sky with the radiance of gold, glowed copper-red in the sun's rays, like a cloud at sunset.

sanskrit: tasyās tad vimalaṃ vaktram ākāśe rāvaṇāṅkagam na rarāja vinā rāmaṃ vinālam iva paṅkajam
english: Her spotless face, borne in Rāvaṇa's lap in the sky, did not shine without Rāma — like a lotus without its stalk.

sanskrit: babhūva jaladaṃ nīlaṃ bhittvā candra ivoditaḥ sulalāṭaṃ sukeśāntaṃ padmagarbhābham avraṇam śuklaiḥ suvimalair dantaiḥ prabhāvadbhir alaṃkṛtam
english: It was as though the moon had risen cleaving a dark cloud: her face with its beautiful brow, lovely hair-line, the splendour of a lotus interior, unblemished, adorned with white, very pure, lustrous teeth.

sanskrit: ruditaṃ vyapamṛṣṭāstraṃ candravat priyadarśanam sunāsaṃ cārutāmrauṣṭham ākāṣe hāṭakaprabham
english: Tear-streaked, her mascara smeared, yet lovely to behold like the moon, with a beautiful nose and charming copper-red lips, she blazed in the sky with a radiance like gold.

sanskrit: rākṣasendrasamādhūtaṃ tasyās tad vacanaṃ śubham śuśubhe na vinā rāmaṃ divā candra ivoditaḥ
english: Her auspicious speech, shaken by the lord of rākṣasas, did not shine without Rāma, like the moon risen by day.

sanskrit: sā hemavarṇā nīlāṅgaṃ maithilī rākṣasādhipam śuśubhe kāñcanī kāñcī nīlaṃ maṇim ivāśritā
english: Maithilī, golden in complexion, shone against the dark-limbed lord of rākṣasas as a golden girdle resting against a sapphire.

sanskrit: sā padmagaurī hemābhā rāvaṇaṃ janakātmajā vidyudghanam ivāviśya śuśubhe taptabhūṣaṇā
english: The daughter of Janaka, lotus-fair and radiant as gold, adorned with burnished ornaments, shone against Rāvaṇa as lightning shining within a dark cloud.

sanskrit: tasyā bhūṣaṇaghoṣeṇa vaidehyā rākṣasādhipaḥ babhūva vimalo nīlaḥ saghoṣa iva toyadaḥ
english: With the jingling of Vaidehī's ornaments, the lord of rākṣasas became like a dark, pure storm-cloud sounding with thunder.

sanskrit: uttamāṅgacyutā tasyāḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ sītāyā hriyamāṇāyāḥ papāta dharaṇītale
english: The shower of flowers fallen from her hair scattered all around and fell to the ground as Sītā was being carried off.

sanskrit: sā tu rāvaṇavegena puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ samādhūtā daśagrīvaṃ punar evābhyavartata
english: But that shower of flowers, scattered all around by the speed of Rāvaṇa's flight, returned and fell again upon Daśagrīva.

sanskrit: abhyavartata puṣpāṇāṃ dhārā vaiśravaṇānujam nakṣatramālāvimalā meruṃ nagam ivottamam
english: A stream of flowers fell back upon the younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa, pure as a garland of stars, as upon the most excellent of mountains, Meru.

sanskrit: caraṇān nūpuraṃ bhraṣṭaṃ vaidehyā ratnabhūṣitam vidyunmaṇḍalasaṃkāśaṃ papāta madhurasvanam
english: An anklet set with jewels slipped from Vaidehī's foot — resembling a circle of lightning and tinkling sweetly — and fell to earth.

sanskrit: tarupravālaraktā sā nīlāṅgaṃ rākṣaseśvaram prāśobhayata vaidehī gajaṃ kaṣyeva kāñcanī
english: Red as the new shoot of a tree, Vaidehī adorned the dark-limbed lord of rākṣasas as a golden girth-strap adorns an elephant.

sanskrit: tāṃ maholkām ivākāśe dīpyamānāṃ svatejasā jahārākāśam āviśya sītāṃ vaiśravaṇānujaḥ
english: The younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa carried Sītā away through the sky, blazing with her own radiance like a great meteor in the heavens.

sanskrit: tasyās tāny agnivarṇāni bhūṣaṇāni mahītale saghoṣāṇy avakīryanta kṣīṇās tārā ivāmbarāt
english: Her ornaments, fire-coloured and jingling, fell scattered to the earth like waning stars dropping from the sky.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ stanāntarād bhraṣṭo hāras tārādhipadyutiḥ vaidehyā nipatan bhāti gaṅgeva gaganāc cyutā
english: The pearl necklace, bright as the lord of stars, that slipped from between Vaidehī's breasts and fell shone like the Gaṅgā fallen from heaven.

sanskrit: utpāta vātābhihatā nānādvija gaṇāyutāḥ mā bhair iti vidhūtāgrā vyājahrur iva pādapāḥ
english: Struck by the blast of Rāvaṇa's passage, the trees teeming with flocks of various birds, their tops shaken, seemed to cry out "Fear not!"

sanskrit: nalinyo dhvastakamalās trastamīnajale carāḥ sakhīm iva gatotsāhāṃ śocantīva sma maithilīm
english: The lotus ponds with their blossoms battered, their fish frightened and darting through the water, seemed to mourn for Maithilī as for a friend who had lost all hope.

sanskrit: samantād abhisaṃpatya siṃhavyāghramṛgadvijāḥ anvadhāvaṃs tadā roṣāt sītācchāyānugāminaḥ
english: Lions, tigers, deer, and birds, rushing together from all sides and then following the shadow of Sītā below, pursued her out of fury.

sanskrit: jalaprapātāsramukhāḥ śṛṅgair ucchritabāhavaḥ sītāyāṃ hriyamāṇāyāṃ vikrośantīva parvatāḥ
english: Their waterfalls like weeping eyes, their peaks like upraised arms, the mountains seemed to cry out aloud as Sītā was being carried off.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇāṃ tu vaidehīṃ dṛṣṭvā dīno divākaraḥ pravidhvastaprabhaḥ śrīmān āsīt pāṇḍuramaṇḍalaḥ
english: Seeing Vaidehī being carried off, the sun himself grew faint, his radiance shattered, the glorious one's disc turning pale.

sanskrit: nāsti dharmaḥ kutaḥ satyaṃ nārjavaṃ nānṛśaṃsatā yatra rāmasya vaidehīṃ bhāryāṃ harati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "There is no dharma, where then is truth? There is no uprightness, no compassion — in a world where Rāvaṇa carries off Rāma's wife Vaidehī."

sanskrit: iti sarvāṇi bhūtāni gaṇaśaḥ paryadevayan vitrastakā dīnamukhā rurudur mṛgapotakāḥ
english: Thus all beings lamented in groups; the young deer, frightened and their faces pitiable, wept.

sanskrit: udvīkṣyodvīkṣya nayanair āsrapātāvilekṣaṇāḥ supravepitagātrāś ca babhūvur vanadevatāḥ
english: Looking up again and again with eyes clouded by falling tears, their bodies trembling greatly, the forest goddesses were overcome with grief.

sanskrit: vikrośantīṃ dṛḍhaṃ sītāṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhaṃ tathā gatām tāṃ tu lakṣmaṇa rāmeti krośantīṃ madhurasvarām
english: Seeing Sītā crying out so loudly and sunk in such grief, crying out "Lakṣmaṇa! Rāma!" in a sweet voice —

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇāṃ bahuṣo vaidehīṃ dharaṇītalam sa tām ākulakeśāntāṃ vipramṛṣṭaviśeṣakām jahārātmavināśāya daśagrīvo manasvinām
english: — Vaidehī, who looked back again and again at the ground below, her hair dishevelled at the ends, her cosmetic marks smeared, was carried off by Daśagrīva to his own destruction, that noble-minded woman.

sanskrit: tatas tu sā cārudatī śucismitā vinākṛtā bandhujanena maithilī apaśyatī rāghavalakṣmaṇāv ubhau vivarṇavaktrā bhayabhārapīḍitā
english: Then she, the beautiful-toothed, pure-smiling Maithilī, bereft of her kinsmen, not seeing Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa, her face drained of colour, tormented by the weight of fear —

sanskrit: kham utpatantaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā maithilī janakātmajā duḥkhitā paramodvignā bhaye mahati vartinī
english: Seeing him soaring into the sky, Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, grieved and utterly terrified, standing in the midst of great fear —

sanskrit: roṣarodanatāmrākṣī bhīmākṣaṃ rākṣasādhipam rudatī karuṇaṃ sītā hriyamāṇedam abravīt
english: — her eyes copper-red with anger and weeping, Sītā, being carried off, addressed the fearsome-eyed lord of rākṣasas in piteous weeping with these words.

sanskrit: na vyapatrapase nīca karmaṇānena rāvaṇa jñātvā virahitāṃ yo māṃ corayitvā palāyase
english: "You feel no shame, O vile Rāvaṇa, for this deed — you who, knowing me to be alone and unprotected, have stolen me and flee."

sanskrit: tvayaiva nūnaṃ duṣṭātman bhīruṇā hartum icchatā mamāpavāhito bhartā mṛgarūpeṇa māyayā yo hi mām udyatas trātuṃ so 'py ayaṃ vinipātitaḥ
english: "Surely it was you yourself, O wicked-souled coward, who, wishing to abduct me, lured away my husband through the illusion of a deer-form; and even this one who rose to protect me has been struck down."

sanskrit: paramaṃ khalu te vīryaṃ dṛśyate rākṣasādhama viśrāvya nāmadheyaṃ hi yuddhe nāsti jitā tvayā
english: "Truly your valour is paramount, O most wretched of rākṣasas — you proclaim your name but in battle there is none whom you have conquered!"

sanskrit: īdṛśaṃ garhitaṃ karma kathaṃ kṛtvā na lajjase striyāś ca haraṇaṃ nīca rahite ca parasya ca
english: "How do you feel no shame having done this most censurable deed — the abduction of another's wife, O vile one, in secret and when she is alone?"

sanskrit: kathayiṣyanti lokeṣu puruṣāḥ karma kutsitam sunṛśaṃsam adharmiṣṭhaṃ tava śauṇḍīryamāninaḥ
english: "Men in the world will proclaim your despicable, most cruel, most unrighteous deed — you who fancy yourself a hero."

sanskrit: dhik te śauryaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca yat tvayā kathitaṃ tadā kulākrośakaraṃ loke dhik te cāritram īdṛśam
english: "Shame on your heroism and your character as you then proclaimed it — a disgrace to your lineage in the world! And shame on conduct such as yours!"

sanskrit: kiṃ śakyaṃ kartum evaṃ hi yaj javenaiva dhāvasi muhūrtam api tiṣṭhasva na jīvan pratiyāsyasi
english: "What can be done if you flee only with speed! Stand even for a moment — you will not return alive!"

sanskrit: na hi cakṣuḥpathaṃ prāpya tayoḥ pārthivaputrayoḥ sasainyo 'pi samartaḥs tvaṃ muhūrtam api jīvitum
english: "Were you to come within sight of those two sons of kings, you would not be capable of living even a moment, even with your whole army."

sanskrit: na tvaṃ tayoḥ śarasparśaṃ soḍhuṃ śaktaḥ kathaṃ cana vane prajvalitasyeva sparśam agner vihaṃgamaḥ
english: "You are no more capable of enduring the touch of their arrows than a bird is capable of enduring the touch of a blazing fire in the forest."

sanskrit: sādhu kṛtvātmanaḥ pathyaṃ sādhu māṃ muñca rāvaṇa matpradharṣaṇaruṣṭo hi bhrātrā saha patir mama vidhāsyati vināśāya tvaṃ māṃ yadi na muñcasi
english: "Do what is beneficial for yourself — release me, O Rāvaṇa. For my husband, angered by the violation done to me, together with his brother, will bring about your destruction if you do not release me."

sanskrit: yena tvaṃ vyavasāyena balān māṃ hartum icchasi vyavasāyaḥ sa te nīca bhaviṣyati nirarthakaḥ
english: "The purpose with which you wish to carry me off by force, O vile one, that purpose of yours will prove fruitless."

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ tam apaśyantī bhartāraṃ vibudhopamam utsahe śatruvaśagā prāṇān dhārayituṃ ciram
english: "Not seeing that husband of mine who is like a god, I, fallen into the enemy's power, cannot bear to sustain my life for long."

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ cātmanaḥ śreyaḥ pathyaṃ vā samavekṣase mṛtyukāle yathā martyo viparītāni sevate
english: "Surely you do not consider what is good or beneficial for yourself, just as a mortal at the hour of death pursues what is contrary to his welfare."

sanskrit: mumūrṣūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ yat pathyaṃ tan na rocate paśyāmīva hi kaṇṭhe tvāṃ kālapāśāvapāśitam
english: "Indeed, for all those who are about to die, what is beneficial does not please them. I seem to see the noose of Time already fastened around your throat."

sanskrit: yathā cāsmin bhayasthāne na bibheṣe daśānana vyaktaṃ hiraṇmayān hi tvaṃ saṃpaśyasi mahīruhān
english: "That you feel no fear in this place of danger, O ten-faced one, evidently you are seeing only trees of gold before your eyes."

sanskrit: nadīṃ vairataṇīṃ ghorāṃ rudhiraughanivāhinīm khaḍgapatravanaṃ caiva bhīmaṃ paśyasi rāvaṇa
english: "You are beholding, O Rāvaṇa, the terrible river Vaitaraṇī flowing with streams of blood, and the dreadful forest whose leaves are swords."

sanskrit: taptakāñcanapuṣpāṃ ca vaidūryapravaracchadām drakṣyase śālmalīṃ tīkṣṇām āyasaiḥ kaṇṭakaiś citām
english: "You shall behold the śālmalī tree, dreadful, studded with sharp iron thorns, its flowers of heated gold, its finest leaves of vaidūrya gem."

sanskrit: na hi tvam īdṛśaṃ kṛtvā tasyālīkaṃ mahātmanaḥ dhārituṃ śakṣyasi ciraṃ viṣaṃ pītveva nirghṛṇaḥ
english: "Having done such a wrong to that great-souled one, you will not be able to sustain yourself for long — like a merciless one who has drunk poison."

sanskrit: baddhas tvaṃ kālapāśena durnivāreṇa rāvaṇa kva gato lapsyase śarma bhartur mama mahātmanaḥ
english: "You are bound by the irresistible noose of Time, O Rāvaṇa — wherever you go, how will you find safety from my husband, that great-souled one?"

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa vinā bhrātaram āhave rākṣasā nihatā yena sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
english: "He who in the mere twinkling of an eye slew fourteen thousand rākṣasas in battle without even his brother —"

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ rāghavo vīraḥ sarvāstrakuśalo balī na tvāṃ hanyāc charais tīkṣṇair iṣṭabhāryāpahāriṇam
english: "— how would that Rāghava, the hero, skilled in all weapons and mighty, not slay you with sharp arrows for stealing his beloved wife?"

sanskrit: etac cānyac ca paruṣaṃ vaidehī rāvaṇāṅkagā bhayaśokasamāviṣṭā karuṇaṃ vilalāpa ha
english: This and much else that was harsh did Vaidehī, sitting in Rāvaṇa's lap, seized by fear and grief, lament pitifully.

sanskrit: tathā bhṛśārtāṃ bahu caiva bhāṣiṇīṃ vilalāpa pūrvaṃ karuṇaṃ ca bhāminīm jahāra pāpas taruṇīṃ viveṣṭatīṃ nṛpātmajām āgatagātravepathum
english: Thus deeply afflicted and speaking many words, having first lamented pitifully, that sinful one carried off the high-spirited young princess, daughter of a king, writhing in his grasp, her body trembling all over.
